subsystems.name: Multimodal perception encoder
subsystems.role: turns camera images, depth, proprioception and touch into a shared representation the policy can reason over.
parts: vision transformer or similar image encoder

subsystems.name: Policy backbone
subsystems.role: the large pretrained network that links what the robot sees and is told to what it should do.

subsystems.name: Action head
subsystems.role: emits the next movement — often a short chunk of future actions rather than a single step.
parts: tokenised action decoder, or a flow-matching / diffusion head for continuous actions

subsystems.name: Robot body and low-level controller
subsystems.role: executes the commanded motion; the model never commands torque directly on real hardware.
parts: whole-body balancing controller for mobile platforms

subsystems.name: Data engine
subsystems.role: supplies the demonstrations the model imitates.

subsystems.name: Inference and safety layer
subsystems.role: runs the model fast enough to control the robot and stops it when unsure.

buildSteps.title: Choose the embodiment
buildSteps.detail: Decide the arm, hand and sensor set, since the action space the model learns is defined by the hardware it will drive.

buildSteps.title: Collect demonstrations
buildSteps.detail: Humans teleoperate or physically guide the robot through hundreds to millions of task attempts, recording video, joint states and instructions together.

buildSteps.title: Standardise the data
buildSteps.detail: Convert recordings from many different robots and cameras into one common schema with consistent action, frame-rate and state conventions, so data can be pooled.

buildSteps.title: Pretrain the backbone
buildSteps.detail: Train or adapt a vision-language model on large image-text corpora plus internet video and robot footage, so it already recognises objects, words and spatial relations.

buildSteps.title: Attach and train the action head
buildSteps.detail: Add the action decoder and train it, usually by imitation learning, so the network outputs movement chunks that reproduce the demonstrated behaviour; some recipes co-train on web data to keep language understanding intact.

buildSteps.title: Fine-tune per task or robot
buildSteps.detail: Adapt the general model to a specific kitchen, warehouse or home with a smaller set of new demonstrations, sometimes refined by reinforcement learning in simulation.

buildSteps.title: Evaluate in simulation, then reality
buildSteps.detail: Score success rates across many randomised scenes, then test on hardware, measuring how often the robot completes the task without help.

buildSteps.title: Deploy with limits
buildSteps.detail: Run inference at control rate, cap speed and force, and keep a monitor that halts the robot when the model is uncertain or the scene is unsafe.

prerequisites.why: they give robots pretrained grounding in objects, words and scenes, which is what makes generalisation possible.

prerequisites.tech: Cheap parallel compute for training and onboard inference
prerequisites.why: these models are far too large to run without accelerators, and training needs thousands of GPU-days.

prerequisites.tech: Affordable dexterous hands and compliant actuators
prerequisites.why: a general policy is only as capable as the body it commands.
pooled data from many labs and robots is what lets one model transfer between embodiments.
simulation provides scale, but contact-rich manipulation still differs enough that real data remains necessary.

prerequisites.tech: Safety and certification standards for learned robot control
prerequisites.why: no accepted framework yet exists for certifying a neural network that decides its own motions around people.

pathway.milestone: research VLA models that follow spoken instructions and perform simple tabletop tasks across several robot types
pathway.unlocks: proof that one model can drive more than one body.

pathway.milestone: models that handle longer, multi-step household tasks with acceptable reliability and low-latency onboard inference
pathway.unlocks: useful home and warehouse assistants for constrained, supervised settings.

pathway.milestone: on-robot learning from its own failures, so new skills need little or no human teleoperation
pathway.unlocks: deployment in unpredictable real environments without constant re-collection of data.

pathway.milestone: certified runtime safety and shared skill libraries across robot fleets
pathway.unlocks: general-purpose robots working alongside people in homes and public spaces.
